correctness.rationale: Properness confines every color class to one multipartite part. If q colors are used and part i uses c_i colors, each vertex in that part totally dominates exactly q-c_i color classes, so the kTD condition is precisely q-c_i>=k. This yields existence iff k<=N-L. Writing t=q-k turns minimization into r<=k+t<=sum_i min(n_i,t), and the converse occupancy construction realizes the minimum. The Stirling-number count follows by allocating labeled colors among parts and counting onto maps. Exhaustive packaged checks agree on all tested instances.
